name: Paris, France (first hot-air balloon flight)
clues: Two men became the first humans ever to fly, lifted by smoke inside a giant bag of cloth and paper. Where did they rise?
The first people ever to fly took off from a royal park in this city, above the Seine. Where am I?
1783: the first manned hot-air balloon flight, in Paris.
fact: The Montgolfier balloon flew about 9 km in 25 minutes before landing outside the city.

name: Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge, New York City
clues: I'm so long that the Earth's curve made my towers lean apart, and I tie an island of boroughs to another. Where am I?
Every November, thousands of marathon runners start their race by crossing me in this city. Where am I?
1964: the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge opens, linking Staten Island and Brooklyn, New York.
fact: Its towers are about 4 cm farther apart at the top than at the bottom because of the Earth's curve.

name: Provincetown Harbor, Cape Cod, USA (Mayflower Compact)
clues: Before they set foot on land, 41 men signed a promise on a ship that was meant to carry wine. Where were they anchored?
The Pilgrims signed their famous rules here, at the hooked tip of a Massachusetts peninsula, before moving on to Plymouth. Where am I?
1620: the Mayflower Compact is signed off the tip of Cape Cod, Massachusetts.
fact: The Mayflower first anchored at Cape Cod, not Plymouth, after more than two months at sea.

name: Dayton, Ohio, USA (Dayton Accords)
clues: A war in Europe ended in a city of the American Midwest, at an air base named after two famous brothers. Where am I?
The birthplace of the aviation pioneers hosted the peace talks that ended the Bosnian War. Where am I?
1995: the Dayton Peace Agreement is initialed at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio.
fact: Leaders spent three weeks locked inside the base until they agreed.

name: UCLA, Los Angeles, USA (first permanent internet link)
clues: Here a computer said "LO" and crashed, yet that broken word grew into the web you're using now. Where am I?
The first permanent link of the internet's ancestor connected a university in this sunny city to Stanford. Where am I?
1969: the first permanent ARPANET link is set up between UCLA in Los Angeles and Stanford.
fact: The first message attempt in October 1969 was meant to be LOGIN, but the system crashed after LO.

name: Dealey Plaza, Dallas, USA
clues: A grassy knoll, a book depository and an open car made a sunny lunchtime the darkest day of a decade. Where am I?
A US president was shot during a parade through downtown in this Texas city. Where am I?
1963: President John F. Kennedy is assassinated in Dealey Plaza, Dallas.
fact: The Texas School Book Depository is now the Sixth Floor Museum.

name: 10 Downing Street, London
clues: The Iron Lady stepped out of a black door with a number on it and said goodbye. Where am I?
Britain's first woman prime minister announced she would resign after 11 years in this address in the UK capital. Where am I?
1990: Margaret Thatcher announces her resignation at 10 Downing Street, London.
fact: The famous black door can't be opened from the outside: it has no keyhole.

name: Reichstag, Berlin, Germany
clues: A scientist who grew up behind a wall became the most powerful woman in Europe, under a glass dome. Where am I?
Angela Merkel was sworn in as chancellor in the parliament of this capital city. Where am I?
2005: Angela Merkel becomes Germany's first female chancellor, in Berlin.
fact: The Reichstag's glass dome lets visitors walk above the lawmakers.

name: Cape of Good Hope, South Africa
clues: Sailors called me the Cape of Storms, but a king renamed me for hope. One explorer slipped past me on his way to India. Where am I?
Vasco da Gama rounded this rocky point near the southern tip of Africa. Where am I?
1497: Vasco da Gama's fleet rounds the Cape of Good Hope, South Africa.
fact: Despite the legend, the Cape of Good Hope is not Africa's southernmost point; Cape Agulhas is.

name: Dumbarton, Scotland (Cutty Sark launched)
clues: I was named after a witch's short shirt in a famous poem, and I raced tea across the world. Where was I born?
The fastest tea clipper was launched on the River Clyde, west of Glasgow. Where am I?
1869: the clipper ship Cutty Sark is launched at Dumbarton, Scotland.
fact: Cutty Sark now sits in dry dock in Greenwich, London.

name: BBC Television Centre, London (Doctor Who)
clues: A man with two hearts first stepped out of a police box that's bigger on the inside. Where was he born?
A time-traveling TV hero first appeared on screens from this capital city, the day after a world-shaking news story. Where am I?
1963: Doctor Who first airs on the BBC in London.
fact: The first episode was repeated the next week because news of JFK's death overshadowed it.

name: New York City (first LIFE magazine)
clues: My first cover showed a giant dam, and for decades I let the world see the news instead of reading it. Where was I printed?
The famous photo magazine LIFE published its first issue in this city of skyscrapers. Where am I?
1936: the first issue of LIFE magazine comes out in New York.
fact: The first cover photo, by Margaret Bourke-White, showed the Fort Peck Dam in Montana.

name: San Francisco, USA (first jukebox)
clues: For a nickel, a box in a saloon played you a song through tubes in your ears. Where did the music start?
The first coin-operated phonograph, the jukebox's ancestor, was put in a saloon in this hilly Californian city. Where am I?
1889: the first jukebox goes into service at the Palais Royale Saloon, San Francisco.
fact: It had no speakers: four people listened through stethoscope-like tubes.

name: Irpinia, near Naples, Italy (1980 earthquake)
clues: On a quiet Sunday evening the mountains east of a famous pizza city shook for over a minute. Where am I?
A huge earthquake struck the hills inland from Naples, in southern Italy. Where am I?
1980: the Irpinia earthquake strikes southern Italy, east of Naples.
fact: It led Italy to create its national civil protection service.

name: Tarawa, Kiribati
clues: A tiny ring of coral near the equator saw one of the bloodiest three days of a world war. Where am I?
The Battle of Tarawa ended on this Pacific atoll, in today's Kiribati. Where am I?
1943: the Battle of Tarawa ends in the Gilbert Islands, now Kiribati.
fact: Kiribati is the only country with islands in all four hemispheres.

name: London (On the Origin of Species published)
clues: A naturalist who sailed on a ship called the Beagle sold out his book in a single day, and it changed how we see apes. Where was it published?
Darwin's famous book on evolution was published in this capital city. Where am I?
1859: Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species is published in London.
fact: All 1,250 copies of the first printing sold out to booksellers on the first day.

name: Tasmania, Australia (Abel Tasman sights it)
clues: A Dutch sailor named me after his boss, but now I carry his own name, and a cartoon devil lives here. Where am I?
Abel Tasman became the first European to sight this island south of mainland Australia. Where am I?
1642: Abel Tasman sights Tasmania, which he named Van Diemen's Land.
fact: The island was renamed Tasmania, after him, in 1856.

name: Hadar, Ethiopia (Lucy found)
clues: My bones were named after a Beatles song playing in the camp, and I'm about 3.2 million years old. Where was I found?
The famous human-ancestor skeleton Lucy was found in the Afar desert of this East African country. Where am I?
1974: the Lucy skeleton is discovered at Hadar, Ethiopia.
fact: The team named her after Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds, which they played that night.

name: Portland to Seattle, USA (D.B. Cooper)
clues: A man in a suit took $200,000, jumped from a plane into the rainy night, and was never seen again. Where did he vanish?
D.B. Cooper parachuted from a hijacked jet over the forests between Portland and Seattle. Where am I?
1971: D.B. Cooper hijacks a flight from Portland and jumps somewhere over southwest Washington.
fact: In 1980 a boy found $5,800 of the ransom money buried by the Columbia River.

name: Tokyo, Japan (first B-29 raid)
clues: A city that had never seen enemy planes in the war looked up at silver giants flying from an island 2,400 km away. Where am I?
The first big US bomber raid hit this capital, flying from Saipan. Where am I?
1944: the first B-29 bomber raid on Tokyo, Japan.
fact: The bombers flew about 2,400 km each way from the Mariana Islands.

name: Havana, Cuba (Fidel Castro dies)
clues: A bearded man in green who survived hundreds of plots against him finally died at 90 in his island capital. Where am I?
Cuba's longtime leader Fidel Castro died in this Caribbean capital. Where am I?
2016: Fidel Castro dies in Havana, Cuba.
fact: Castro led Cuba for almost 50 years.

name: SARM Studios, London (Band Aid)
clues: In one day, dozens of pop stars squeezed into one studio to ask if Africa knew it was Christmas. Where am I?
The Band Aid charity single was recorded in a studio in this capital city. Where am I?
1984: the Band Aid single is recorded at SARM Studios in London.
fact: It became the UK's best-selling single for over a decade.

name: Manhattan, New York City (Evacuation Day)
clues: The last redcoats sailed away, but left a flag on a greased pole for the Americans to fight with. Where am I?
British troops finally left this city at the end of the American Revolution. Where am I?
1783: the British evacuate New York City, ending the occupation.
fact: A sailor climbed the greased flagpole to tear down the British flag.

name: Arlington National Cemetery, near Washington DC
clues: A little boy saluted his father, and an eternal flame was lit on a hill across the river from the capital. Where am I?
President Kennedy was buried here, in a cemetery across the Potomac from Washington DC. Where am I?
1963: John F. Kennedy is buried at Arlington National Cemetery.
fact: It was his son John Jr.'s third birthday.

name: Barfleur, Normandy, France (White Ship)
clues: A drunken crew wrecked a king's only son, and England fell into 19 years of chaos. Where did the ship go down?
The White Ship sank off a Normandy harbor, drowning the heir to the English throne. Where am I?
1120: the White Ship sinks off Barfleur, Normandy.
fact: Only one person, a butcher from Rouen, survived.

name: Valley of the Kings, Luxor, Egypt
clues: "Can you see anything?" "Yes, wonderful things!" A boy king's gold glittered in candlelight for the first time in 3,000 years. Where am I?
Howard Carter opened Tutankhamun's tomb in this royal desert valley across the Nile from Luxor. Where am I?
1922: Howard Carter first looks into Tutankhamun's tomb, Valley of the Kings, Egypt.
fact: The tomb held more than 5,000 objects.

name: Maui, Hawaii (Captain Cook arrives)
clues: A captain who mapped half the world sighted a valley isle in the Pacific during the whale season. Where am I?
Captain James Cook first sighted this Hawaiian island, the second largest in the chain. Where am I?
1778: Captain James Cook sights Maui, Hawaii.
fact: Maui's Haleakalā volcano rises over 3,000 m.

name: Oxford, England (Alice in Wonderland)
clues: A math teacher told a girl about a white rabbit on a boat trip, and the book came out on this day. Where did the story begin?
Lewis Carroll created Alice's Adventures in Wonderland for a girl in this university city. Where am I?
1865: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland is published; it was born in Oxford.
fact: Alice Liddell was the daughter of the dean of Christ Church, Oxford.

name: Heathrow Airport, London (Brink's-Mat robbery)
clues: Robbers came for cash but found three tonnes of gold bars next to the world's busiest runway. Where am I?
The Brink's-Mat robbery happened at a warehouse by the main airport of this capital. Where am I?
1983: the Brink's-Mat gold robbery at Heathrow Airport, London.
fact: Most of the gold was never found.

name: Hammaguir, Algeria (France's first satellite)
clues: A satellite named after a comic-book Gaul flew from the Sahara, making a country the third in space. Where am I?
France launched its first satellite, Astérix, from a desert base in this North African country. Where am I?
1965: France launches Astérix, its first satellite, from Hammaguir, Algeria.
fact: Only the USSR and the US had launched satellites before.

name: Macy's, New York City (first Thanksgiving parade)
clues: Lions, bears and camels from a zoo marched down the avenues to a store's front door. Where am I?
The first Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade marched through this city. Where am I?
1924: the first Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, New York City.
fact: The first parade used live animals from the Central Park Zoo instead of balloons.

name: Seattle, USA (Jimi Hendrix born)
clues: A left-handed boy who'd later play a right-handed guitar upside down was born in a rainy port city. Where am I?
Jimi Hendrix was born in this city of the Pacific Northwest. Where am I?
1942: Jimi Hendrix is born in Seattle.
fact: Hendrix learned on a one-string ukulele he found in the trash.

name: Paris, France (Nobel's will)
clues: A man who invented a blast wrote a will at a club that turned his fortune into peace. Where did he write it?
Alfred Nobel signed the will creating the Nobel Prizes in this European capital. Where am I?
1895: Alfred Nobel signs his will at the Swedish-Norwegian Club in Paris.
fact: His family was stunned to learn most of his fortune went to the prizes.

name: Clermont-Ferrand, France (First Crusade called)
clues: A pope stood in a field of volcanoes and the crowd shouted "God wills it!" Where am I?
Pope Urban II called the First Crusade at a council in central France. Where am I?
1095: Pope Urban II calls the First Crusade at Clermont, France.
fact: The city is now home to the Michelin tire company.

name: Toulon, France (fleet scuttled)
clues: A navy sank itself in its own harbor so the enemy couldn't sail it. Where am I?
The French fleet was scuttled in this Mediterranean naval port. Where am I?
1942: the French fleet scuttles itself at Toulon.
fact: More than 70 ships were sunk.

name: Nashville, USA (Grand Ole Opry)
clues: A radio barn dance became the longest-running radio show in America, in a city of guitars. Where am I?
The Grand Ole Opry first went on air in this Tennessee city. Where am I?
1925: the Grand Ole Opry's first broadcast, Nashville.
fact: The Opry has aired every week since 1925.

name: Wellington, New Zealand (women vote)
clues: A country at the bottom of the world let all women vote first in a national election. Where am I?
Women voted in a national election for the first time in this country; its capital is here. Where am I?
1893: New Zealand women vote in a national election, the first in the world.
fact: Suffragist Kate Sheppard is on New Zealand's $10 note.

name: Tehran, Iran (Tehran Conference)
clues: Three war leaders met for the first time in a city below snowy mountains to plan D-Day. Where am I?
Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin first met together in this Middle Eastern capital. Where am I?
1943: the Tehran Conference begins.
fact: Roosevelt stayed at the Soviet embassy for security.

name: London (Royal Society founded)
clues: Twelve men met after a lecture and founded a club whose motto means "take nobody's word for it." Where am I?
The Royal Society, the world's oldest science academy, was founded in this city. Where am I?
1660: the Royal Society is founded at Gresham College, London.
fact: Isaac Newton later became its president.

name: Strait of Magellan, Chile
clues: An explorer called an ocean "peaceful" after a terrifying 38-day maze of channels. Where did he escape?
Magellan's ships came out of this strait near the tip of South America into the Pacific. Where am I?
1520: Magellan's fleet enters the Pacific through the Strait of Magellan.
fact: Magellan named the Pacific for its calm waters.

name: Barcelona, Spain (FC Barcelona founded)
clues: A Swiss man placed an ad in a newspaper and founded a club that's "more than a club." Where am I?
FC Barcelona was founded in this Mediterranean city. Where am I?
1899: FC Barcelona is founded.
fact: Its founder was Joan Gamper, who was Swiss.

name: San Jose, California, USA (founded)
clues: I began as a farm town for a Spanish mission, and now I'm the capital of a valley named after a chip. Where am I?
The first civilian town in Spanish California was founded here; now it's Silicon Valley's biggest city. Where am I?
1777: San Jose is founded as California's first Spanish civilian town.
fact: San Jose was California's first state capital.

name: Belfast, Northern Ireland (C.S. Lewis born)
clues: A boy who would write about a wardrobe, a lion and a witch was born in a city famous for building a doomed ship. Where am I?
C.S. Lewis, author of Narnia, was born in this city in Northern Ireland. Where am I?
1898: C.S. Lewis is born in Belfast.
fact: Belfast's shipyard also built the Titanic.

name: Albuquerque, USA (Microsoft named)
clues: Two young men named their software company in a letter, in a desert city of hot-air balloons. Where am I?
The name Micro-soft was first used in this New Mexico city, where the company began. Where am I?
1975: Bill Gates and Paul Allen first use the name Micro-soft, in Albuquerque.
fact: Microsoft moved to the Seattle area in 1979.

name: Germantown, Philadelphia, USA (Louisa May Alcott born)
clues: The woman who wrote about four sisters, Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy, was born in a city of liberty and cheesesteaks. Where am I?
Little Women author Louisa May Alcott was born in this Pennsylvania city. Where am I?
1832: Louisa May Alcott is born in Germantown, Philadelphia.
fact: She shared her birthday with her father.

name: Glasgow, Scotland (first international football match)
clues: The first international football match ended 0-0, on a cricket ground on a saint's day. Where am I?
Scotland and England played the first official international football match in this Scottish city. Where am I?
1872: Scotland v England, the first international football match, Glasgow.
fact: About 4,000 people watched.

name: Barbados
clues: I'm a Caribbean island that became free on this day, and a pop star with an umbrella grew up here. Where am I?
This easternmost Caribbean island became independent from Britain. Where am I?
1966: Barbados becomes independent.
fact: Rihanna is from Barbados.

name: Blenheim Palace, England (Churchill born)
clues: A war leader was born early, in a palace, during a party. Where am I?
Winston Churchill was born in this huge palace near Oxford. Where am I?
1874: Winston Churchill is born at Blenheim Palace.
fact: Blenheim is the only non-royal house in England called a palace.

name: Crystal Palace, London
clues: A giant house of glass burned so bright that people saw the glow 80 km away. Where am I?
The Crystal Palace, a huge glass hall, burned down in this city. Where am I?
1936: the Crystal Palace burns down, London.
fact: It was first built in Hyde Park for the Great Exhibition of 1851.

name: Sylacauga, Alabama, USA (meteorite)
clues: A woman napping on her couch was hit by a stone from space. Where am I?
The only confirmed person hit by a meteorite was in this town in Alabama. Where am I?
1954: a meteorite hits Ann Hodges in Sylacauga, Alabama.
fact: She was bruised but fine.

name: Montgomery, Alabama, USA (Rosa Parks)
clues: She changed history by refusing to stand up, sitting tired on a city bus. Where am I?
Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat in the capital of Alabama. Where am I?
1955: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama.
fact: Her arrest started the Montgomery bus boycott, which lasted 381 days.

name: English Channel (Channel Tunnel breakthrough)
clues: An English digger and a French digger shook hands through a hole, 40 meters under the sea. Where am I?
Workers from Britain and France met for the first time under this sea channel, in the tunnel between them. Where am I?
1990: Channel Tunnel workers from England and France break through and meet.
fact: The tunnel is about 50 km long, 38 km of it under the sea.

name: Highland Park, Detroit, USA (Ford assembly line)
clues: Cars started moving past the workers instead of the workers moving around the cars, and a car took 90 minutes instead of 12 hours. Where am I?
Henry Ford started his moving assembly line in this Michigan car city. Where am I?
1913: Ford's moving assembly line starts at Highland Park, in the Detroit area.
fact: The Model T came in any color, Ford joked, as long as it's black.

name: Washington DC, USA (Antarctic Treaty)
clues: Twelve nations agreed that a whole continent belongs to no one and is only for penguins and science. Where did they sign?
The Antarctic Treaty was signed in the capital of the United States. Where am I?
1959: the Antarctic Treaty is signed in Washington DC.
fact: It bans military activity and mining in Antarctica.

name: San José, Costa Rica (army abolished)
clues: A leader smashed a fortress wall with a hammer and handed the keys to a museum. His country has had no army since. Where am I?
Costa Rica abolished its army in its capital city. Where am I?
1948: Costa Rica abolishes its army, in San José.
fact: The old army headquarters is now the National Museum.

name: Notre-Dame, Paris, France (Napoleon crowned)
clues: The pope came all the way to crown him, but he grabbed the crown and put it on himself. Where am I?
Napoleon crowned himself emperor in the great cathedral of this capital. Where am I?
1804: Napoleon crowns himself emperor at Notre-Dame, Paris.
fact: The painting of the scene by Jacques-Louis David is almost 10 m wide.

name: Dubai, UAE (United Arab Emirates formed)
clues: Six desert sheikhdoms became one country in a house by the sea, and a seventh joined soon after. Where am I?
The United Arab Emirates was born in a building in this Gulf city, now famous for the world's tallest tower. Where am I?
1971: the United Arab Emirates is formed, signed at Union House in Dubai.
fact: Ras Al Khaimah joined as the seventh emirate in February 1972.

name: University of Chicago, USA (first nuclear chain reaction)
clues: Under the seats of a football stadium, scientists started the first atomic chain reaction. Where am I?
The first controlled nuclear chain reaction happened in this windy Midwest city. Where am I?
1942: the first controlled nuclear chain reaction, Chicago Pile-1.
fact: The message sent afterward was a code: "The Italian navigator has landed in the New World."

name: Salt Lake City, USA (first permanent artificial heart)
clues: A dentist lived 112 days with a plastic heart that clicked so loudly people could hear it. Where am I?
The first permanent artificial heart was put in a patient at a university in the capital of Utah. Where am I?
1982: Barney Clark gets the first permanent artificial heart, Salt Lake City.
fact: The Jarvik-7 heart was powered by an air compressor.

name: Austerlitz (Slavkov), Czechia
clues: On the first anniversary of his crowning, an emperor beat two other emperors in the fog. Where am I?
Napoleon's greatest victory, the Battle of the Three Emperors, was fought near Brno in today's Czechia. Where am I?
1805: Napoleon wins the Battle of Austerlitz.
fact: A Paris train station, Gare d'Austerlitz, is named after it.

name: Tokyo, Japan (PlayStation launches)
clues: A gray box with a circle, a cross, a square and a triangle went on sale, and gamers lined up for hours. Where am I?
The first Sony PlayStation went on sale in this capital city. Where am I?
1994: the PlayStation launches in Japan.
fact: It sold about 100,000 units on its first day.

name: Cape Town, South Africa (first heart transplant)
clues: A surgeon gave a man a new heart below a mountain with a flat top. Where am I?
The first human heart transplant happened at a hospital in this South African city. Where am I?
1967: Christiaan Barnard performs the first human heart transplant, Cape Town.
fact: The hospital, Groote Schuur, now has a museum about it.

name: Newbury, England (first text message)
clues: A 22-year-old engineer typed "Merry Christmas" on a computer, and phones have never stopped buzzing. Where am I?
The first text message was sent to a phone at a company in this English town west of London. Where am I?
1992: the first SMS text message, "Merry Christmas," is sent in Newbury, England.
fact: The phone couldn't reply, because phones couldn't send texts yet.

name: Ballarat, Australia (Eureka Stockade)
clues: Gold miners built a wooden fort and raised a blue flag with stars. Where am I?
The Eureka Rebellion happened in this gold-rush town in Victoria, Australia. Where am I?
1854: the Eureka Stockade rebellion in Ballarat, Australia.
fact: The Eureka flag is still a symbol of protest in Australia.

name: Berdychiv, Ukraine (Joseph Conrad born)
clues: A boy who learned English in his twenties grew up to write it like a master, and was born far from any sea. Where am I?
Joseph Conrad, author of Heart of Darkness, was born in this town in today's Ukraine. Where am I?
1857: Joseph Conrad is born in Berdychiv, now in Ukraine.
fact: Conrad was a sailor for about 20 years before writing.

name: Sun Studio, Memphis, USA (Million Dollar Quartet)
clues: A king, a man in black, a wild piano man and a rockabilly star jammed together by chance. Where am I?
Elvis, Johnny Cash, Jerry Lee Lewis and Carl Perkins played together at a small studio in this Tennessee city. Where am I?
1956: the Million Dollar Quartet session at Sun Studio, Memphis.
fact: The recording sat unheard for over 20 years.

name: Miami, USA (first Burger King)
clues: A king who sells burgers started his kingdom in a city of beaches and palms. Where am I?
The first Burger King restaurant under that name opened in this Florida city. Where am I?
1954: the first Burger King opens in Miami.
fact: The Whopper arrived in 1957.

name: London (The Observer first published)
clues: I'm the oldest Sunday newspaper in the world, and I've been watching since 1791. Where was I born?
The Observer, the world's oldest Sunday paper, was first printed in this capital. Where am I?
1791: The Observer is first published in London.
fact: Its founder hoped to get rich, but quickly ran into debt.

name: Berkeley Hundred, Virginia, USA (Thanksgiving)
clues: English settlers gave thanks two years before the Pilgrims, and Virginia still says it was first. Where am I?
A day of thanksgiving was held at this plantation on the James River in Virginia in 1619. Where am I?
1619: settlers hold a day of thanksgiving at Berkeley Hundred, Virginia.
fact: Their orders said the day should be kept every year.

name: Atlantic Ocean, between the Azores and Portugal (Mary Celeste)
clues: A ship sailed on with no one aboard, food still in the stores, and no one ever learned why. Where was she found?
The ghost ship Mary Celeste was found drifting between the Azores and Portugal. Where am I?
1872: the Mary Celeste is found abandoned in the Atlantic.
fact: Arthur Conan Doyle wrote a famous (made-up) story about her.

name: Vienna, Austria (Mozart dies)
clues: A genius died at 35 while writing music for the dead, and nobody knows where he's buried. Where am I?
Mozart died in this capital city of music while writing his Requiem. Where am I?
1791: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart dies in Vienna.
fact: He was buried in an unmarked grave in St. Marx Cemetery.

name: Chicago, USA (Walt Disney born)
clues: A boy who'd draw a famous mouse was born in a windy city, not in a castle. Where am I?
Walt Disney was born in this big city on Lake Michigan. Where am I?
1901: Walt Disney is born in Chicago.
fact: His family moved to a farm in Missouri when he was four.

name: Bermuda Triangle, off Florida (Flight 19)
clues: Five planes flew out on a training flight, their compasses spun, and none ever came back. Where did they vanish?
Flight 19 disappeared in the ocean area off Florida known as the Bermuda Triangle. Where am I?
1945: Flight 19 vanishes off Florida, starting the Bermuda Triangle legend.
fact: A rescue plane sent to find them also disappeared.

name: Môle-Saint-Nicolas, Haiti (Columbus reaches Hispaniola)
clues: An admiral found a big island and named it after his own country. Where did he land?
Columbus reached the island of Hispaniola at the tip of today's Haiti. Where am I?
1492: Christopher Columbus reaches Hispaniola, at today's Haiti.
fact: Hispaniola is shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

name: Salt Lake City, USA (Prohibition ends)
clues: A state where many people don't drink cast the deciding vote to bring drinking back. Where am I?
Utah's vote ended Prohibition in the US, in its capital city. Where am I?
1933: Utah ratifies the 21st Amendment in Salt Lake City, ending Prohibition.
fact: Prohibition had lasted almost 14 years.

name: Washington Monument, Washington DC
clues: My tip is aluminum, which was rarer than silver then, and I'm a different color halfway up. Where am I?
The giant obelisk in the US capital was finished with its capstone on this day. Where am I?
1884: the Washington Monument is completed in Washington DC.
fact: The color changes because building stopped for over 20 years and new stone was used.

name: Quito, Ecuador (founded)
clues: I'm a capital city built near the middle of the world, high in the mountains. Where am I?
Spanish settlers founded this Andean capital near the equator. Where am I?
1534: Quito, Ecuador, is founded by the Spanish.
fact: Quito is about 2,850 m above sea level.

name: Halifax, Canada (Halifax Explosion)
clues: Two ships collided in a harbor and made the biggest man-made blast before the atomic bomb. Where am I?
The Halifax Explosion hit this port city in Nova Scotia, Canada. Where am I?
1917: the Halifax Explosion, Nova Scotia.
fact: Halifax still sends Boston a Christmas tree every year to thank it for its help.

name: Edinburgh, Scotland (Encyclopaedia Britannica)
clues: Three men set out to write down everything there is to know, in a city with a castle on a volcano. Where am I?
The first part of the Encyclopaedia Britannica came out in this Scottish capital. Where am I?
1768: the Encyclopaedia Britannica's first part is published in Edinburgh.
fact: Britannica stopped printing in 2012 and went online only.

name: Menlo Park, New Jersey, USA (Edison's phonograph)
clues: A man who couldn't hear well recorded "Mary had a little lamb" and played it back. Where am I?
Edison recorded his voice on the first phonograph at his lab in this New Jersey village. Where am I?
1877: Thomas Edison records on his phonograph at Menlo Park, New Jersey.
fact: Edison was called the Wizard of Menlo Park.

name: Pearl Harbor, Hawaii
clues: A Sunday morning on a peaceful island ended in "a date which will live in infamy." Where am I?
Japan's surprise attack on the US fleet happened at this Hawaiian naval base. Where am I?
1941: the attack on Pearl Harbor, Hawaii.
fact: The USS Arizona Memorial sits above the sunken ship.

name: Cape Canaveral, Florida (Apollo 17)
clues: The last people to walk on the Moon set off at night from here, and on the way took the famous Blue Marble photo. Where am I?
Apollo 17 launched from this spaceport on Florida's Atlantic coast. Where am I?
1972: Apollo 17 launches from Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
fact: It was the only Apollo launch at night.

name: New York City (New York Philharmonic's first concert)
clues: The oldest orchestra in America played its very first note, in a city that never sleeps. Where am I?
The New York Philharmonic gave its first concert in this city. Where am I?
1842: the New York Philharmonic gives its first concert.
fact: It played Beethoven's Fifth Symphony.

name: Covent Garden, London (Royal Opera House opens)
clues: A theater opened in a fruit-and-vegetable market and became home to a royal opera. Where am I?
The theater that became the Royal Opera House opened in this London district. Where am I?
1732: the theater that became the Royal Opera House opens in Covent Garden, London.
fact: The market around it ran until 1974.

name: Dover, Delaware, USA (first state)
clues: A small state said yes to the new Constitution before anyone else, so it's always called first. Where am I?
Delaware became the first US state to ratify the Constitution; its capital is here. Where am I?
1787: Delaware becomes the first state to ratify the US Constitution.
fact: Delaware's nickname is the First State.

name: The Dakota, New York City
clues: A musician who asked us to imagine peace was killed outside his building beside a famous park. Where am I?
John Lennon was shot outside his apartment building in this city. Where am I?
1980: John Lennon is killed outside the Dakota, New York City.
fact: The Strawberry Fields memorial in Central Park is across the street.

name: Vatican City, Rome (Second Vatican Council ends)
clues: For three years, bishops from every land met under a famous dome and changed the Mass. Where am I?
The Second Vatican Council closed in St. Peter's Square, in this city. Where am I?
1965: the Second Vatican Council ends in Rome.
fact: Afterward Mass could be said in local languages instead of Latin.

name: Vienna, Austria (Beethoven's 7th premiere)
clues: A composer going deaf conducted his Seventh Symphony, and the crowd made him play a part again. Where am I?
Beethoven's Seventh Symphony was first performed in this capital of music. Where am I?
1813: Beethoven's Seventh Symphony premieres in Vienna.
fact: The slow second part was so loved it was encored that night.

name: White House, Washington DC (INF Treaty)
clues: Two leaders who once aimed missiles at each other agreed to destroy a whole class of them. Where am I?
Reagan and Gorbachev signed the INF Treaty in the White House. Where am I?
1987: Reagan and Gorbachev sign the INF Treaty in Washington DC.
fact: It was the first treaty to wipe out a whole type of nuclear weapon.

name: Belovezha Forest, Belarus (end of the USSR)
clues: In a hunting lodge in an ancient forest of bison, three leaders signed away a superpower. Where am I?
The deal ending the Soviet Union was signed in a forest on the Belarus and Poland border. Where am I?
1991: the Belovezha Accords end the USSR.
fact: The forest is home to Europe's largest herd of wild bison.

name: Geneva, Switzerland (smallpox eradicated)
clues: Experts announced that a disease that killed hundreds of millions was gone from Earth, in a city by a lake. Where am I?
The World Health Organization certified smallpox was wiped out at its headquarters in this Swiss city. Where am I?
1979: experts certify the eradication of smallpox, Geneva.
fact: It is the only human disease ever wiped out.

name: San Francisco, USA (Mother of All Demos)
clues: A man showed off the mouse, video calls and links, in 1968. Where am I?
Douglas Engelbart gave the Mother of All Demos in this Californian city. Where am I?
1968: Douglas Engelbart's Mother of All Demos, San Francisco.
fact: The first mouse was a wooden box with two wheels.

name: Manchester, England (Coronation Street)
clues: The world's longest-running TV soap began on a street that doesn't exist, in a rainy northern city. Where am I?
Coronation Street first aired from a TV studio in this English city. Where am I?
1960: Coronation Street first airs from Manchester.
fact: It has more than 11,000 episodes.

name: Warsaw, Poland (Lech Wałęsa elected)
clues: An electrician who climbed a shipyard fence became his nation's first freely elected president. Where am I?
Lech Wałęsa was elected president of Poland; this is its capital. Where am I?
1990: Lech Wałęsa is elected president of Poland.
fact: Wałęsa won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1983.

name: Ayacucho, Peru
clues: A battle in the Andes ended Spain's rule over South America. Where am I?
The Battle of Ayacucho was fought in the highlands of Peru. Where am I?
1824: the Battle of Ayacucho, Peru.
fact: Ayacucho means "corner of the dead" in Quechua.

name: Stockholm, Sweden (first Nobel Prizes)
clues: On the anniversary of his death, a dynamite maker's fortune was handed out for the first time. Where am I?
The first Nobel Prizes were given in this Scandinavian capital. Where am I?
1901: the first Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm.
fact: The Peace Prize is given in Oslo instead.

name: Paris, France (Universal Declaration of Human Rights)
clues: Across the river from an iron tower, the world wrote down 30 rights that belong to everyone. Where am I?
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted in this capital city. Where am I?
1948: the Universal Declaration of Human Rights is adopted in Paris.
fact: It's the most translated document in the world.

name: Westminster, London (first traffic light)
clues: The first traffic light ran on gas, had arms like a railway signal, and blew up a month later. Where am I?
The world's first traffic light was put up outside Parliament in this city. Where am I?
1868: the first traffic light is installed in Westminster, London.
fact: It exploded in January 1869, injuring the policeman running it.

name: Aswan, Egypt (Aswan Dam opens)
clues: A dam was built on the world's longest river, near the islands of an ancient temple. Where am I?
The first Aswan Dam opened on the Nile in southern Egypt. Where am I?
1902: the first Aswan Dam opens on the Nile.
fact: The later High Dam created Lake Nasser.

name: Amherst, Massachusetts, USA (Emily Dickinson born)
clues: A poet who rarely left her house wrote nearly 1,800 poems, most found only after she died. Where was she born?
Emily Dickinson was born in this college town in Massachusetts. Where am I?
1830: Emily Dickinson is born in Amherst, Massachusetts.
fact: Fewer than a dozen of her poems were published while she was alive.

name: Kyoto, Japan (Kyoto Protocol)
clues: In a city of a thousand temples, the world first promised to cut the gases warming the planet. Where am I?
The Kyoto Protocol on climate change was adopted in this old Japanese capital. Where am I?
1997: the Kyoto Protocol is adopted in Kyoto, Japan.
fact: It came into force in 2005.

name: New York City (UNICEF created)
clues: After a world war, a fund was set up to help children everywhere, by a river in a city of skyscrapers. Where am I?
UNICEF was created by the United Nations, headquartered in this city. Where am I?
1946: UNICEF is created by the UN in New York.
fact: UNICEF won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965.

name: Windsor Castle, England (Edward VIII abdicates)
clues: A king gave up his crown for the woman he loved and told the nation by radio from a castle. Where am I?
Edward VIII broadcast his abdication speech from this royal castle west of London. Where am I?
1936: Edward VIII broadcasts his abdication from Windsor Castle.
fact: He married Wallis Simpson, an American divorcée, in 1937.

name: Westminster, London (Statute of Westminster)
clues: A law let Canada, Australia and New Zealand make their own laws, passed in a palace by the Thames. Where am I?
The Statute of Westminster was passed in the Parliament of this city. Where am I?
1931: the Statute of Westminster is passed in London.
fact: It made the dominions equal partners with Britain.

name: Clausthal, Germany (Robert Koch born)
clues: A doctor who found the germ behind tuberculosis was born in a mining town in mountains of witches. Where am I?
Robert Koch was born in this town in Germany's Harz Mountains. Where am I?
1843: Robert Koch is born in Clausthal, Germany.
fact: Koch won the Nobel Prize in 1905.

name: Basilica of Guadalupe, Mexico City
clues: Roses bloomed in winter, and a picture appeared on a farmer's cloak on a hill in a big capital. Where am I?
The Virgin of Guadalupe is said to have appeared on a hill in this city, now home to her basilica. Where am I?
1531: the image of the Virgin of Guadalupe appears, by tradition, in Mexico City.
fact: Millions of pilgrims visit the basilica every December 12.

name: Nairobi, Kenya (Kenya independence)
clues: At midnight a new flag went up and a city near giraffes and lions became a free nation's capital. Where am I?
Kenya became independent; its capital is here. Where am I?
1963: Kenya becomes independent.
fact: Nairobi has a national park with lions inside the city limits.

name: Signal Hill, St. John's, Canada (Marconi's transatlantic signal)
clues: With a kite in a storm, a man heard three clicks that had crossed an ocean through the air. Where am I?
Marconi got the first radio signal across the Atlantic on a hill in Newfoundland. Where am I?
1901: Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal at Signal Hill, Newfoundland.
fact: The signal was the letter S in Morse code.

name: Hoboken, New Jersey, USA (Frank Sinatra born)
clues: Ol' Blue Eyes was born across the river from the city he sang about, New York, New York. Where am I?
Frank Sinatra was born in this New Jersey city facing Manhattan. Where am I?
1915: Frank Sinatra is born in Hoboken, New Jersey.
fact: He weighed about 6 kg at birth.

name: San Luis Obispo, California, USA (first motel)
clues: Halfway between two big cities, a hotel for cars was born and gave us a new word. Where am I?
The world's first motel opened in this town between Los Angeles and San Francisco. Where am I?
1925: the Milestone Mo-Tel, the first motel, opens in San Luis Obispo.
fact: A room cost $1.25 a night.

name: Carnegie Hall, New York City (An American in Paris)
clues: Real taxi horns played in a concert about France, in a city across the ocean. Where am I?
Gershwin's An American in Paris premiered in a famous concert hall in this city. Where am I?
1928: George Gershwin's An American in Paris premieres at Carnegie Hall, New York.
fact: Gershwin brought real Paris taxi horns home for it.

name: Malta (becomes a republic)
clues: A tiny island country between Sicily and Africa said goodbye to the British queen as its head of state. Where am I?
Malta became a republic; it's an island nation in the middle of the Mediterranean. Where am I?
1974: Malta becomes a republic.
fact: Malta is one of the smallest countries in the EU.

name: Plymouth, England (Drake sets sail)
clues: A sea dog left a port city and came back nearly three years later, having sailed around the world. Where am I?
Francis Drake set out on his voyage around the world from this port in southwest England. Where am I?
1577: Francis Drake sets sail from Plymouth to circle the globe.
fact: Legend says Drake finished a game of bowls here before facing the Spanish Armada.

name: West Reading, Pennsylvania, USA (Taylor Swift born)
clues: A girl who grew up on a Christmas tree farm and later filled stadiums was born in a small town in the Keystone State. Where am I?
Taylor Swift was born near Reading, in Pennsylvania. Where am I?
1989: Taylor Swift is born in West Reading, Pennsylvania.
fact: Her family owned a Christmas tree farm.

name: Trento, Italy (Council of Trent opens)
clues: Church leaders met for 18 years in a mountain city to answer Martin Luther. Where am I?
The Council of Trent opened in this city in the Italian Alps. Where am I?
1545: the Council of Trent opens in Trento, Italy.
fact: It met on and off until 1563.

name: South Pole (Amundsen arrives)
clues: Five men and their dogs reached a place where every direction is north, and beat a rival by 34 days. Where am I?
Roald Amundsen's team was the first to reach the bottom of the world. Where am I?
1911: Roald Amundsen reaches the South Pole.
fact: Scott's team arrived on January 17, 1912, and found the Norwegian flag.

name: Mount Vernon, Virginia, USA (George Washington dies)
clues: The first president died at home on a hill above a river near the capital that carries his name. Where am I?
George Washington died at his estate on the Potomac, south of Washington DC. Where am I?
1799: George Washington dies at Mount Vernon, Virginia.
fact: His last words were reportedly "'Tis well."

name: Berlin, Germany (quantum theory)
clues: A physicist said energy comes in tiny packets, and the quantum age began in a capital on the Spree. Where am I?
Max Planck presented his quantum theory in this German capital. Where am I?
1900: Max Planck presents his quantum theory in Berlin.
fact: Planck's constant is now used to define the kilogram.

name: Glasgow, Scotland (Glasgow Subway opens)
clues: The world's third-oldest underground train runs in one simple circle, so you can't get lost. Where am I?
The Glasgow Subway opened in this Scottish city. Where am I?
1896: the Glasgow Subway opens.
fact: Locals call it the Clockwork Orange because of its orange trains.

name: Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, France (Nostradamus born)
clues: A man famous for predicting the future was born in a Provençal town where Van Gogh would later paint. Where am I?
Nostradamus was born in this town in Provence, France. Where am I?
1503: Nostradamus is born in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence.
fact: Van Gogh painted The Starry Night in a hospital there.

name: Atlanta, USA (Gone with the Wind premiere)
clues: A film about a city that burned premiered in the same city, rebuilt, with a three-day party. Where am I?
Gone with the Wind premiered in the capital of Georgia. Where am I?
1939: Gone with the Wind premieres in Atlanta.
fact: Hattie McDaniel, who won an Oscar for the film, was not allowed into the segregated premiere.

name: Leaning Tower of Pisa, Italy (reopens)
clues: After ten years shut, engineers straightened me a little, but not too much, or no one would come. Where am I?
The famous leaning bell tower reopened after repairs in this Tuscan city. Where am I?
2001: the Leaning Tower of Pisa reopens after being partly straightened.
fact: Engineers reduced the lean by about 45 cm.

name: Les Invalides, Paris (Napoleon's return)
clues: An emperor who died on a far-off island came home nearly 20 years later under a golden dome. Where am I?
Napoleon's body was brought back from Saint Helena and laid to rest in this Paris monument. Where am I?
1840: Napoleon's remains arrive at Les Invalides, Paris.
fact: His tomb is made of red quartzite.

name: Anzio, Italy (Nero born)
clues: A Roman emperor who was said to play music while his city burned was born in a seaside town. Where am I?
Emperor Nero was born in Antium, today's Anzio, on the coast south of Rome. Where am I?
37 AD: Emperor Nero is born in Antium, today's Anzio, Italy.
fact: The fiddle story is a myth: fiddles didn't exist yet.

name: Dijon, France (Gustave Eiffel born)
clues: The man behind Paris's iron tower and the Statue of Liberty's skeleton was born in a city famous for mustard. Where am I?
Gustave Eiffel was born in this city in Burgundy, France. Where am I?
1832: Gustave Eiffel is born in Dijon.
fact: He also designed the inner frame of the Statue of Liberty.

name: Boston, USA (Boston Tea Party)
clues: People dressed in disguise made the biggest cup of tea ever, and it wasn't to drink. Where am I?
Colonists dumped British tea into the harbor of this Massachusetts city. Where am I?
1773: the Boston Tea Party.
fact: The 342 chests of tea would be worth about $1.7 million today.

name: Bonn, Germany (Beethoven born)
clues: A composer who couldn't hear his own symphonies was born in a city that later became a country's capital. Where am I?
Beethoven was born in this city on the Rhine, West Germany's former capital. Where am I?
1770: Ludwig van Beethoven is born in Bonn (baptized the next day).
fact: Beethoven's birth house in Bonn is now a museum.

name: Bastogne, Belgium (Battle of the Bulge)
clues: Surrounded in the snow and told to surrender, a general answered with one word: "Nuts!" Where am I?
The Battle of the Bulge began in the Ardennes forest, centered on this Belgian town. Where am I?
1944: the Battle of the Bulge begins in the Ardennes.
fact: It was the biggest US battle of World War II.

name: Dhaka, Bangladesh (Victory Day)
clues: A nation won its freedom on the banks of a giant delta, and celebrates its Victory Day today. Where am I?
Bangladesh won its independence war; its capital is here. Where am I?
1971: Bangladesh wins its war of independence, Dhaka.
fact: Bangladesh is one of the most densely populated countries in the world.

name: Steventon, England (Jane Austen born)
clues: The author of Pride and Prejudice was born in a village rectory in the south of England. Where am I?
Jane Austen was born in this Hampshire village. Where am I?
1775: Jane Austen is born in Steventon, Hampshire.
fact: She's on the Bank of England £10 note.

name: Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, USA (first powered flight)
clues: Two bicycle makers flew for 12 seconds on a windy beach, and the world got smaller. Where am I?
The Wright brothers made the first powered flight on the Outer Banks of North Carolina. Where am I?
1903: the Wright brothers' first powered flight, Kitty Hawk.
fact: The first flight was shorter than a Boeing 747's wingspan.

name: Buenos Aires, Argentina (Pope Francis born)
clues: The first pope from the Americas was born in a city of tango. Where am I?
Pope Francis was born in Argentina's capital. Where am I?
1936: Jorge Mario Bergoglio, later Pope Francis, is born in Buenos Aires.
fact: He once worked as a nightclub bouncer.

name: Zócalo, Mexico City (Aztec Sun Stone found)
clues: Workers fixing a city square dug up a giant stone calendar that the Aztecs had carved. Where am I?
The Aztec Sun Stone was found under the main square of this capital. Where am I?
1790: the Aztec Sun Stone is found in the Zócalo, Mexico City.
fact: It weighs about 24 tonnes.

name: Berlin, Germany (nuclear fission)
clues: Two chemists split an atom and found it was the key to unlocking enormous energy. Where am I?
Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann discovered nuclear fission in this German capital. Where am I?
1938: nuclear fission is discovered in Berlin.
fact: Lise Meitner explained the result but was left out of Hahn's Nobel Prize.

name: Sidi Bouzid, Tunisia (Arab Spring begins)
clues: A fruit seller's protest in a small town sparked revolutions across a whole region. Where am I?
The Arab Spring began in this town in central Tunisia. Where am I?
2010: Mohamed Bouazizi's protest in Sidi Bouzid, Tunisia, starts the Arab Spring.
fact: Tunisia's president fled less than a month later.

name: Lusail, Qatar (Argentina wins the World Cup)
clues: A little genius finally lifted the golden trophy, after a final with a hat-trick, in a desert stadium. Where am I?
Messi's Argentina won the World Cup final in a stadium in this Gulf country. Where am I?
2022: Argentina wins the World Cup at Lusail Stadium, Qatar.
fact: The final ended 3-3, and Argentina won on penalties.

name: Mariinsky Theatre, St. Petersburg, Russia (The Nutcracker)
clues: A Christmas ballet with dancing candy and a toy soldier was first danced in a city of canals and white nights. Where am I?
Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker premiered in this Russian city on the Baltic. Where am I?
1892: The Nutcracker premieres in St. Petersburg.
fact: It flopped at first and only became a Christmas classic decades later.

name: Cincinnati, USA (Steven Spielberg born)
clues: The director of a shark film, a lost alien and a dinosaur park was born on the Ohio River. Where am I?
Steven Spielberg was born in this Ohio city. Where am I?
1946: Steven Spielberg is born in Cincinnati.
fact: He was rejected from film school more than once.

name: Geological Society, London (Piltdown Man announced)
clues: Scientists cheered the "missing link", but its skull was human and its jaw was an ape's. The hoax lasted 40 years. Where was it announced?
The Piltdown Man hoax was presented to scientists in this capital city. Where am I?
1912: Piltdown Man is announced at the Geological Society, London.
fact: The hoax was exposed in 1953.

name: Achères, France (first land speed record)
clues: An electric car set the first land speed record, at 63 km/h, near Paris. Where am I?
The first official land speed record was set in this town west of Paris. Where am I?
1898: the first land speed record is set at Achères, France.
fact: The car was electric, not gasoline.

name: London (A Christmas Carol published)
clues: Three ghosts visited a mean old man, and in six days his book sold out in a foggy city. Where am I?
Charles Dickens's A Christmas Carol was published in this capital. Where am I?
1843: A Christmas Carol is published in London.
fact: Dickens wrote it in about six weeks.

name: Paris, France (Édith Piaf born)
clues: The Little Sparrow, who sang that she regretted nothing, was born in a city of love. Where am I?
Édith Piaf was born in the Belleville district of this capital. Where am I?
1915: Édith Piaf is born in Paris.
fact: Piaf means "sparrow" in Paris slang.

name: Williamsburg Bridge, New York City
clues: When it opened, I was the longest suspension bridge on Earth, beating my famous neighbor to the south. Where am I?
The Williamsburg Bridge opened over the East River in this city. Where am I?
1903: the Williamsburg Bridge opens in New York City.
fact: It was the first big suspension bridge with steel towers.

name: Valley Forge, Pennsylvania, USA
clues: A tired army spent a freezing winter in huts, and came out stronger. Where am I?
George Washington's army made its winter camp here, northwest of Philadelphia. Where am I?
1777: Washington's army arrives at Valley Forge.
fact: A Prussian officer, von Steuben, drilled the troops there.

name: Hanoi, Vietnam (Indochina War begins)
clues: A city of lakes went dark and a war for independence began that lasted eight years. Where am I?
The First Indochina War began with fighting in Vietnam's capital. Where am I?
1946: the First Indochina War begins in Hanoi.
fact: It ended with the battle of Dien Bien Phu in 1954.

name: Macau
clues: A city of casinos and old Portuguese streets became the last European colony in Asia to be handed back. Where am I?
Portugal handed this territory near Hong Kong back to China. Where am I?
1999: Portugal hands Macau back to China.
fact: Macau's casinos earn more than Las Vegas.

name: New York City (It's a Wonderful Life premiere)
clues: A film about an angel earning wings flopped when it came out, then became a Christmas classic. Where did it premiere?
It's a Wonderful Life premiered in this city. Where am I?
1946: It's a Wonderful Life premieres in New York City.
fact: It became a classic after its copyright lapsed and TV channels played it every Christmas.

name: New Orleans, USA (Louisiana Purchase)
clues: A flag came down in a square by the Mississippi, and the United States doubled in size. Where am I?
The US took over the Louisiana Purchase in a ceremony in this city. Where am I?
1803: the Louisiana Purchase is handed over in New Orleans.
fact: The US paid about 3 cents an acre.

name: Charleston, South Carolina, USA (secession)
clues: A state left the Union, and the first shots of the war came months later in its own harbor. Where am I?
South Carolina left the Union at a convention in this port city. Where am I?
1860: South Carolina secedes from the Union in Charleston.
fact: The Civil War started at Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor.

name: Arco, Idaho, USA (first nuclear electricity)
clues: Four light bulbs lit up using atoms in a desert lab. Where am I?
The first electricity from nuclear power was made at a lab near this Idaho town. Where am I?
1951: the first nuclear electricity lights four bulbs near Arco, Idaho.
fact: In 1955 Arco became the first town powered by nuclear energy.
